statements.t: The Company continued to invest responsibly in infrastructure projects that enhance quality and reliability for customers, including water main replacements, groundwater wells, and water quality treatment projects.
The Company expects to close the Nevada and Oregon acquisitions in the fourth quarter of 2026.

With the long-term debt agreements and equity forward arrangements in place, the Company believes it has the resources to finance its on-going initiatives into the first half of 2027, including the acquisition of Nevada and Oregon systems which we expect to close before December 31, 2026.
The Company’s 59 th consecutive annual dividend increase announced earlier this year is expected to yield an annual dividend of $1.34 per common share, an increase of 8.1% over 2025.
These ongoing efforts are expected to better prepare the Company to deal with natural disasters, including wildfires and forecasted El Niño conditions.

For additional details on the Company’s third quarter results, please see the Form 10-Q which will be available at: www.calwatergroup.com/investors/financials-filings-reports/sec-filings , or listen to the earnings teleconference or teleconference replay.

risks.t: our ability to invest or apply the proceeds from the issuance of common stock in an accretive manner
our ability to complete [the issuance of the Notes and Bonds and] the settlement of the forward sales agreements on the expected timing or at all]
consequences of eminent domain actions relating to our water systems
increased risk of inverse condemnation losses as a result of the impact of weather, climate change and natural disasters, including wildfires and landslides
shifts in population, including housing and customer growth
issues with the implementation, maintenance or security of our information technology and operational technology systems
physical and cyber security risks and threats and the adequacy of our efforts to mitigate such risks and threats
the ability of our enterprise risk management processes to identify or address risks adequately
labor relations matters as we negotiate with the unions
changes in customer water use patterns and the effects of conservation, including as a result of drought conditions
risks associated with expanding our business and operations, including into other geographic areas
the impact of market conditions and volatility on unrealized gains or losses on our non-qualified benefit plan investments and our operating results
the impact of weather and timing of meter reads on our accrued and unbilled revenue
the impact of evolving legal and regulatory requirements, including sustainability requirements
other risks and unforeseen events described in our Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) filings
